AlternateTargets: what meets the eye is awakening
Senses.Explanation: Masters raise ‘awakening wherever the eye lands’ as a public question, then enact or redirect the answer through an immediately visible object or action without making one response universal. The graphs say “meet or strike the eye” and “awakening”: “awakening wherever the eye meets.” The exact question “What is awakening wherever the eye meets?” accounts for 69 of the headword’s 127 occurrences. The answers and follow-up actions vary. When Shishuang Qingzhu asks Daowu, Daowu calls a novice, tells him to add water to the clean-water jar, later asks Shishuang what he had just asked, and leaves as Shishuang begins to repeat it; the narrative then says Shishuang woke up. Another exchange answers, “All things constantly abide”; when asked what that means, the named record subject answers with the headword again. Elsewhere the answer is “the buddha hall before you,” a named record subject kicks a dog so that it runs off making a sound, or Xuansha says, “Before a dead monk is precisely awakening wherever the eye meets.” Linquan’s later comment on the Daowu case says that it has “no empty gap.” The records preserve these named exchanges and different predicates; this entry gives no single explanation in place of their different answers.
Senses.Note: The headword occurs 127 times in 58 allowlisted texts. The direct question occurs 69 times in 31 texts, while Xuansha’s line about the dead monk occurs 8 times in 8. The related saying “what meets the eye is the Way” occurs 7 times in 7 texts. The case witnesses must not be collapsed: Daowu’s novice-and-water-jar exchange, the reciprocal “all things constantly abide” answer, the buddha-hall answer, the kicked-dog action, and Xuansha’s dead-monk statement are distinct recorded deployments.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師後參道吾問。如何是觸目菩提。道吾喚沙彌。沙彌應諾。吾曰。添淨缾水著。吾却問師。汝適來問什麼。師乃舉前問道吾便起去。師從此惺覺。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (景德傳燈錄), Shishuang Qingzhu section. Shishuang Qingzhu is the exact questioner who asks Daowu Yuanzhi, ‘what is awakening upon contact with the eyes?’ Daowu calls a novice, sends him to add water to the bottle, and walks away after Shishuang repeats the question.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有人問：「如何是觸目菩提？」師答曰：「一切法常住。」「如何是一切法常住？」師曰：「觸目菩提。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Ancestor Hall Collection (祖堂集): Cen Heshang answers the question 'what is awakening wherever the eye meets?' first with 'all things constantly abide' and then by repeating the headword.

Occurrences.Kwic: 亡僧面前正是觸目菩提。萬里神光頂後相。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (景德傳燈錄), Xuansha Shibei section. Xuansha Shibei is the exact teaching-seat speaker who says that directly before a dead monk is precisely awakening upon contact with the eyes. Xuefeng Yicun is Xuansha's lineage teacher, not the speaker here.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問如何是觸目菩提。師曰。面前佛殿。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (景德傳燈錄), Tongan Daopi section. An unnamed monk questioning Tongan Daopi is the exact speaker who asks what awakening upon contact with the eyes is; Tongan answers, ‘the buddha hall before you.’ All six attribution rungs leave the monk personally unnamed; Yunju Daoying is the lineage ancestor, not the actor.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有僧問如何是觸目菩提。師踢狗子作聲走。僧無對。師曰。小狗子不消一踢。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (景德傳燈錄), Taiyuan Fu section. An unnamed monk questioning Taiyuan Fu is the exact speaker who asks what awakening upon contact with the eyes is; Taiyuan kicks a dog so that it runs off yelping. All six attribution rungs leave the monk unnamed; Xuefeng Yicun is not the actor.

Occurrences.Kwic: 以此觀來，觸目菩提無空缺處，更嫌何處不分明？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Empty Hall Collection (林泉老人評唱丹霞淳禪師頌古虗堂集): in his comment on the Daowu-Shishuang case, Linquan Conglun says awakening wherever the eye meets has no empty gap.

Occurrences.Kwic: 歸方丈。溈至晚。上堂曰。大眾。米裡有蟲。諸人好看。後參道吾。問。如何是觸目菩提。吾喚沙彌。彌應諾。吾曰。添淨瓶水著。良久却問師。汝適來問甚麼。師擬舉。吾便起去。師於此有省。吾將順世。垂語曰
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (五燈會元). The quoted case explicitly assigns the headword-bearing question to Shishuang Qingzhu; the present document merely raises the earlier exchange.
